output.summary: The rise in ED length of stay for admitted patients is almost entirely boarding (about 3.0 of 3.2 hours). Boarding jumped in March 2026, when the hospitalist rounding change took effect. After it, before-noon medical-ward discharges fell from 29% to 9%. ED RN hours per visit, vacancy and grid compliance were flat. Capacity, occupancy and ED work-up time were also flat. A huddle pilot with a schedule-determined, comparable control cut boarding from 4.6 to 2.3 hours. Extend the huddle. Do not fund travel nurses by deferring case managers, and do not pull the 4 West huddle. Longer door-to-provider time and left-without-being-seen are confounded by the May discontinuation of triage providers. The evening bed-cleaning cut is unmeasured.
